set.text: Every summer, Kenji and his family travel to a small island. They go by boat, and the trip across the sea takes two hours. There, they climb a tall hill. From the top, the view is beautiful. Kenji can see blue water all around him. He takes a photo to send to his grandma.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “view” mean?
options: what you can see from a place
qs.why: From the top of the hill, Kenji sees blue water all around. That is what you can see from a place. “View” can also mean an idea, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “travel” mean?
options: go from one place to another
qs.why: The family goes from home to the island by boat. They do not stay home.

qs.q: How does Kenji's family get to the island?
qs.why: The passage says “They go by boat,” and the trip is across the sea. It does not talk about a car, a plane, or a train.

why: Idea-question why claimed a car or train 'could not' take them, which the passage does not say.

set.text: Mia is a student in the fifth grade. On Friday, she has a math test. All week, she studies at the kitchen table. Some of the problems are difficult, so her big brother helps her. On Monday, the teacher hands back the papers. Her hard work has a good result: 98 out of 100! Nearly every answer is right.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “difficult” mean?
qs.why: Her brother helps her because some problems are hard. “Easy” is the opposite.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “nearly” mean?
options: every single one, with no mistakes
qs.why: She gets 98 out of 100, so almost every answer is right, but not all of them.

qs.q: How did Mia do on the test?
options: she got a perfect score with no mistakes
very well, with only a small mistake
she did badly because she did not study
qs.why: Her hard work gives her 98 out of 100: very good, but not perfect. A careless reader may pick a perfect score.

why: 'result' was used as a test score, not the card meaning 'what happens because of something else'; now the result of her hard work.

set.text: Jada and her friends have a plan: a picnic in the park. They sit outside on a big blanket. Then dark clouds come, and rain starts. They cover the food with a towel and run quickly to a small café. Inside, they eat their sandwiches by the window and watch the rain.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “cover” mean?
qs.why: They put a towel over the food so the rain does not get it wet.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “quickly” mean?
qs.why: Rain starts, so they run fast to the café. “Slowly” is the opposite.

qs.q: Why do Jada and her friends go to the café?
options: because it is too hot outside
qs.why: Dark clouds come and rain starts, so they run inside. They still eat their sandwiches, so they did not forget the food.

why: Opening 'Their plan is...' used 'their' before anyone was named; unclear for Starter readers.

set.text: Today is sports day at school. Five kids line up on the track for a race. Kim is small, but she is very fast. When they start, she runs at top speed. At first, two boys are in front, and Kim is behind. Then, little by little, she gets closer. In the final few steps, she passes them both and wins!

qs.q: In the passage, what does “track” mean?
options: a mark left by a foot
qs.why: The kids line up on it to run the race. “Track” can also be a mark from a foot, but not here.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “final” mean?
qs.why: She passes the boys at the end and wins, so it is the last part of the race.

qs.q: How does Kim win the race?
options: she is first from the start
she passes the two boys near the end
qs.why: At first she is behind two boys, and she passes them in the last part. She is not first from the start.

why: 'behind' (card: adverb) was used as a preposition ('behind two boys'); now used as an adverb.

set.text: Sara's brother, Ali, works in a foreign country. He is far away, but they talk every week. Today is his birthday, so Sara sends him a text: “Happy birthday! How are you?” An hour later, she gets his answer: “I am great, thank you! I hope to visit soon.” Sara smiles. His message makes her very happy.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “foreign” mean?
options: of a country that is not their own
qs.why: Ali works in a country that is not Sara and Ali's own country.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “text” mean?
options: a written message sent by phone
qs.why: Sara writes a short message and sends it to Ali's phone. They do not talk with voices this time.

qs.q: Why does Sara send Ali a text today?
qs.why: The passage says “Today is his birthday,” so she writes “Happy birthday!”

why: 'answer' (card: what you say back to a question) replied to 'Happy birthday!', which is not a question; added a question. Also removed the idiom 'makes her day' (too hard for Starter).

set.text: Every Thursday, Ms. Diaz takes her class to the library. Each child makes a list of books to look for. Lin is learning a new language, Spanish. She finds a book in English and Spanish with a funny title: Cats Do Not Like Hats. On the first page, she knows only one Spanish word: gato. It means cat.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “title” mean?
options: the first word in a book
the person who wrote the book
qs.why: Cats Do Not Like Hats is the name of the book.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “language” mean?
options: the words people use to speak and write
qs.why: Spanish is the new set of words Lin is learning to speak and write.

qs.q: How much Spanish does Lin know?
options: a lot; she reads the whole book easily
she speaks it at home every day
very little; she knows only one word on the first page
she is the best in her class
she teaches it to Ms. Diaz
qs.why: She knows only one Spanish word on the first page, so she knows very little Spanish so far.

why: Contradiction: Lin picks a Spanish book but its title was in English and she knew only one Spanish word; now a book in English and Spanish.

set.text: Tonight, Jamal and his aunt drive far from the city, where the sky is very dark. They lie on a blanket and look up at the night sky. “Each star is a sun, very far from the earth,” his aunt says. For a moment, they are quiet. Then a small light moves across the sky. “Perhaps it is a plane,” says Jamal.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “Perhaps” mean?
qs.why: Jamal is not sure what the light is, so he says maybe.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “dark” mean?
qs.why: Far from the city there are few lights, so the sky has little light. “Bright” is the opposite.

qs.q: Why do Jamal and his aunt drive far from the city?
options: because the city is too cold
to find a dark place to look at the stars
qs.why: They go where the sky is very dark and look up at the night sky. With no city lights, the stars are easier to see. Nothing in the passage is about catching a plane.

why: Idea answer/why claimed they 'see many stars', which the passage never says; reworded to what the text supports.

set.text: Grandpa Joe is 80, and he wants to learn about the internet. His granddaughter Aisha helps him. First, she shows him a website with news. He reads an article about baseball. Then she teaches him to make online video calls. “This is easy!” he says. “I am a modern man now!” Now he calls his old friends every Sunday.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “online” mean?
options: on an old phone with a cord
qs.why: He makes video calls on the internet, not face to face.

qs.q: In the passage, what does “modern” mean?
qs.why: Grandpa is joking that he now uses new things from today, like video calls.

qs.q: What does Grandpa do every Sunday now?
options: he reads about baseball at the library
he talks with his old friends by video
qs.why: The last sentence says “Now he calls his old friends every Sunday,” using what Aisha taught him.

why: 'online' (card: adjective) was used as an adverb ('talk to people online'); now 'online video calls'.
